basic_identification.full_title: Textiles — Resistance to Ignition of Curtains and Drapes — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Textiles Protective Clothing (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Textiles Protective Clothing Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for the resistance to ignition of textile curtains or drapes or their fabrics for use in public places/buildings as per the classification given in Annex B. Curtains and drapes intended for domestic use or transport are explicitly excluded from the scope of this standard.

amendment_slips.description: Completely replaces several clauses of the original standard—including the Foreword, Clause 1.1, Clause 4.1, Clause 4.2, and Clause 5 (comprising 5.1, 5.2, and 5.3)—to define the resistance parameters specifically for public spaces, update the durability and laundering procedures, establish a maximum Toxicity Index of 1.0, and specify sampling and conformity guidelines.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Protective Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (including the Quality Control Amendment Order, 2024) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all textile-based curtains and drapes intended for use in public, residential, or institutional interiors must conform to IS 15741:2007 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India. Products manufactured solely for export are exempt if they conform to foreign buyers' specifications. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial technical textiles or fire-resistant drapes.

requirements.detail: Every roll or prefabricated piece of curtains and drapes conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Curtains or drapes must satisfy specified ignition-resistance thresholds given in Table 1 when tested against defined categories of hazardous public places/buildings as specified in Annex B. Other quality requirements must satisfy relevant Indian Standards or be mutually agreed upon.

The flame-retardant properties of the curtains, drapes, or their fabrics must remain fully effective, satisfying specified ignitability limits after undergoing a minimum of 50 laundering cycles as per the standard washing procedure (Clause C-5) or reduced washing procedure (Clause C-6).

During laundering, ballast consisting of single-layer rectangular pieces of woven 100 percent bleached cotton or 100 percent polyester must be added. Each piece must measure at least 350 × 500 mm and be hemmed along the cut edges to prevent unravelling.

Preliminary laundering calculations require specific machine settings. Type A1 machines: drum volume 70 L, dry test load mass 4.2 ± 0.3 kg, low dip volume 21.0 ± 1.5 L, high dip volume 38.0 ± 3.0 L, and detergent mass 21.0 ± 1.5 g. Type A2 machines: drum volume 45 L, dry test load mass 2.7 ± 0.2 kg, low dip volume 13.5 ± 1.0 L, high dip volume 24.5 ± 2.0 L, and detergent mass 13.5 ± 1.0 g.
requirements.clause_reference: Annex C, Clause C-4.1, C-4.2 & C-4.6

requirements.detail: Load the machine to computed test load mass (m1) with soft water to low dip level (L) at 15 °C to 40 °C, and add low-foaming reference detergent (m2) mixed with perborate immediately before use (1 part perborate to 4 parts detergent). If the inlet water is below 37 °C, heat to 40±3 °C with no agitation, then heat to 75±3 °C in 15±3 min with reduced agitation. Run at 75±3 °C for 15±0.5 min with normal agitation and drain. Fill with cold soft water to high dip level (H), run for 3 min, and drain; repeat this rinsing sequence three more times (total of four rinses). Centrifuge for 6 min. This entire wash-rinse-centrifuge cycle must be repeated 49 times to achieve a total of 50 complete cycles.
requirements.clause_reference: Annex C, Clauses C-2.4, C-5.1 to C-5.4

requirements.requirement_type: Maximum Toxicity Index of Gaseous Eruptions (Clause 4.3)
requirements.detail: The Toxicity Index of gases evolved during the complete burning of 100 g of curtains, drapes, or their fabrics must be a maximum of 1.0.

requirements.requirement_type: Toxicity Index Summations and Chambers (Annex D)
requirements.detail: The toxicity index is a numerical summation of the toxicity factors of selected gases produced by complete combustion under flaming conditions in excess air inside an airtight chamber of at least 1 m³ (approximately 100 × 100 × 100 cm³) lined with opaque plastic. The summation factors are derived based on each gas concentration fatal to man in a 30-minute exposure time. A total index of 1.0, on average, brings about death in 30 minutes.
requirements.clause_reference: Annex D, Clauses D-2.1, D-3 & D-4.1

requirements.detail: The mathematical toxicity calculations utilize the following specific fatal exposure levels (in ppm) to determine individual gas factors: Carbon dioxide (100,000 ppm), Carbon monoxide (4,000 ppm), Hydrogen sulphide (750 ppm), Ammonia (750 ppm), Formaldehyde (500 ppm), Hydrogen chloride (500 ppm), Acrylonitrile (400 ppm), Sulphur dioxide (400 ppm), Nitrogen oxides (250 ppm), Phenol (250 ppm), Hydrogen cyanide (150 ppm), Hydrogen bromide (150 ppm), Hydrogen fluoride (100 ppm), and Phosgene (25 ppm).

requirements.requirement_type: Testing Burner and Flame Boundary Controls (Annex D)
requirements.detail: Testing must be conducted at an air temperature of 27 ± 2 °C. Fabric specimens (normally 3) must be cut to sizes that will be entirely engulfed in the flame. Test pieces are suspended over a Bunsen burner (125 mm overall height, 11 mm bore burner tube, and 5 mm bore gas and air inlet tubes) established at a flow rate of 10 L/min gas and 15 L/min air. The burner is ignited and extinguished from outside using a separate small pin flame. The specimen is subjected to a calibrated flaming temperature of 1150 ± 50 °C. To prevent sample losses from melting or dripping, specimens can be supported on a thin bed of glass wool placed over the wire support mesh.
requirements.clause_reference: Annex D, Clauses D-4.2.2, D-4.2.3, D-5.1, D-9.1 to D-9.5

requirements.requirement_type: Lot Sampling and Criteria for Conformity
requirements.detail: All rolls, pieces, or curtains of identical type manufactured under similar conditions and supplied against a single dispatch note constitute a lot. Random samples must be selected as per col 2 and col 3 of Table 2 to test for ignitability and laundering durability. All samples must meet specified parameters for the lot to be declared conforming.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15741 : 2007 is the strict national Indian Standard safety specification regulating the ignition resistance, thermal durability, and toxicity limits of textile-based curtains, drapes, and their fabrics used in public buildings, offices, and institutions. Under the mandatory national Protective Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all such curtains and drapes must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Following Amendment No. 1 (March 2014), the standard enforces rigorous testing controls: a mandatory 50-cycle laundering durability process utilizing highly specified automatic washing machine parameters (including specific water dips, low-foaming detergent, and woven ballast) to verify long-term fire retardance, and a strict Toxicity Index limit of 1.0 Max on combustion gases (including carbon monoxide, formaldehyde, phosgene, and cyanides) completely burned at 1150 °C to prevent lethal gas buildup in public spaces during a fire.
